parts.text: Sulfur is a Group VI element.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) A sample of sulfur contains two isotopes, 32 S and 34 S.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Complete Table 5.1 to show the number of protons and neutrons in one atom of each isotope of sulfur. Table 5.1 32 S 34 S protons neutrons [2]

parts.label: v
parts.text: (v) Table 5.2 shows the relative abundance of these isotopes of sulfur in the sample. Table 5.2 atom 32 S 34 S relative abundance 95% 5% Calculate the relative atomic mass of sulfur in this sample to one decimal place. relative atomic mass = .............................. [2]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Sulfur reacts with magnesium to form magnesium sulﬁde, MgS, an ionic compound.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Complete the dot-and-cross diagram in Fig. 5.1 of the ions in magnesium sulﬁde. Give the charges on the ions. Fig. 5.1 [3]

ms.label: 5(b)(i)
ms.text:
M1 eight crosses in second shell of Mg
M2 6 dots and 2 cross in third shell of S
M3 ‘2+’ charge on Mg on correct answer line
and ‘2–’ charge on S on correct answer line

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) An acid containing sulfur reacts with sodium hydroxide, NaOH, to form a salt and water. The salt has the formula Na 2 SO 3 .

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Na 2 SO 3 is oxidised by acidiﬁed aqueous potassium manganate( VII ).

ms.label: 5(d)(i)
ms.text: the oxidation number of manganese / Mn is +7
